 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Commonly used to describe fine ceramic or porcelain dinnerware. The term "**China" is derived from the country of China.**
 
• The production of ceramics in China dates back to around **18,000 BCE**. The country is known as the **birthplace of porcelain**.
 
• The **chemical composition of china** (or porcelain) is primarily based on **kaolin, feldspar, and quartz,** with variations for specific types like bone china.
 
• High-quality china dishes are** durable and resistant to chipping**, making them suitable for everyday use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of China:**

 
 
• **Porcelain**: Made from kaolin clay, feldspar, and quartz, porcelain is fired at high temperatures, resulting in a strong, durable, and translucent finish.
 
• **Bone China**: A type of porcelain that includes bone ash, making it lighter and more chip-resistant than standard porcelain.
 
• **Stoneware**: Made from denser clay, stoneware is fired at high temperatures, resulting in a robust product often used for everyday items.
 
 
 
• Chinaware—**primarily includes the following components**:
 
 
• **Kaolin** (Alumina Silicate): Al₂Si₂O₅(OH)₄
 
• **Feldspar**: KAlSi₃O₈ (for potassium feldspar), NaAlSi₃O₈ (for sodium feldspar), CaAl₂Si₂O₈ (for calcium feldspar).
 
• **Quartz** (Silica): SiO₂
 
• **Bone Ash** (for Bone China): Primarily composed of calcium phosphate (Ca₃(PO₄)₂).
